summary: A Florida Forest Fire Lookout Association report names a DeLeon Springs tower that John Seifert operated; no source found dates it or says whether it stands.

facts.status_note: No source found says whether the DeLeon Springs tower stands today, or whether it is open to visitors.

evidence.supports: Seifert moved to Florida and operated the Deleon Springs tower, then the Seville fire tower
evidence.quote: Seifert had moved to the State and operated the Deleon Springs tower and then the Seville fire tower

evidence.supports: Early FFLA work by Seifert produced a working list of Florida lookouts in 1991
evidence.quote: It was through John's first efforts that a working list of Florida lookouts was first obtained in 1991

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts DeLeon Springs page gives its county as Volusia County

sources.title: Florida Chapter report on remaining fire lookouts, 2015 and beginning 2016
sources.publisher: Forest Fire Lookout Association, Florida Chapter

notes_for_editor: The only tower-specific evidence is one sentence in a Florida chapter report that says Seifert operated a Deleon Springs tower. The report does not date it or describe it, so no event is recorded. The Forest Lookouts page for DeLeon Springs has only a heading and county, with no text. Story is about 88 words, below the 120-word floor, for lack of evidence. Searches found no build date, height, design or site description, and the Wikipedia article on DeLeon Springs does not mention a tower. Searches also turned up towerdex antenna registrations in DeLeon Springs, which are telecom structures and not lookouts. Florida Memory returned 403. Access and agency are unknown and are not asserted.
